alias-ref: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `ref p @ pattern`: K's #as binds the matched term itself; remove `ref`
alias-inside-itself: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: identifier `p` is bound more than once in the same pattern: an alias cannot occur inside its own subpattern (E0416)
alias-remainder: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `p @ ..`: a `..` remainder binds only inside a sequence, collection or cells! pattern
alias-in-result: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `name @ pattern` binds only on a left-hand side (K's #as is LHS-only); refer to the name without `@` here
alias-whole-subject: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `p @ pattern` cannot alias a whole rule subject: its root is the matched constructor or function; alias a subterm instead
or-unequal-binders: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: variable `x` is not bound in all alternatives
or-ambiguous: error[krs::analysis::ambiguous-or-pattern]: alternatives `Pair(x, y)` and `Pair(y, x)` of this or-pattern can match the same term with different bindings; K's #Or then is ambiguous (LLVM takes one, Haskell explores both). Make them disjoint or split the rule.
or-in-result: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `|` is a pattern alternative; for Bool disjunction use bool::or or k::or_bool!
matches-shadow: error[krs::analysis::invalid-matches]: `e` in k::matches! binds a new variable; it does not compare with the rule's `e`. Use int::eq/bool::eq, or write `_`
matches-guard: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: K's :=K has no guard; conjoin a separate condition with bool::and
matches-std: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: did you mean `k::matches!`? std's matches! tests a host value
matches-lhs: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `k::matches!` is a Bool test (K's :=K); it cannot appear on a left-hand side or inside a pattern
matches-alias-result: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `p @ pattern` in a `k::matches!` pattern is allowed only in requires and ensures conditions: K rejects #as in a rule's right-hand side
matches-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-matches]: the pattern has sort `Color` and the subject has sort `Exp`, which share no subsort, so this test is always false
matches-claim: error[krs::rust-expansion::uncoded-error]: `k::matches!` is not supported in claims: the pinned native prover cannot resolve K's :=K in a claim; match the shape in the claim's subject instead
